scope.c: v1.2.6 / EBUR128_MODE_I / default L,R / non-histogram / unchanged history limit / add_frames_float / loudness_global
preconditions: New valid states; no reset, allocation failure, history truncation or upstream error.
Every input call succeeds; buffer lengths, frame counts and layout are correct.
Do not infer numeric equality, finite loudness, accuracy, conformance or normative superiority.

static_findings.claim: At 48 kHz both selected schedules form the first complete 400 ms window at 19200 frames and another every 4800 frames. Counts are before gating, not stored or accepted block counts.
Rust finish computes cached integrated loudness, discards an incomplete 100 ms sub-block and seals the instance. C global queries stored block energy without sealing or clearing unfinished input.
Rust uses strict LKFS-domain > gates; selected non-histogram C path uses inclusive energy-domain >= gates. No concrete PCM was shown to reach an equality branch or produce different library outputs.
Two sequential Rust biquads, combined C filter coefficients and distinct energy/loudness arithmetic do not establish bitwise numerical equivalence. No numerical difference was measured.

hypothetical_input.left: 0.25 for even n; -0.25 for odd n
hypothetical_input.right: 0.125 for even floor(n/2); -0.125 for odd floor(n/2)
hypothetical_input.notes: All amplitudes are exactly representable in f32. This is not an official or calibrated loudness reference.

recipes.name: Fresh-state prefix comparison
recipes.calls: Fresh state per prefix and per library; identical f32 samples; Rust finish then getter; C add then global query.
recipes.observe: Return status and numeric category separately; complete window counts are static, LUFS values unknown.

recipes.name: One-shot versus chunked input
recipes.calls: Use fresh states, compare one-shot and split input, Rust finish only after the last chunk.
recipes.observe: Tail retention across successful input calls; actual chunked numeric equality remains untested.

recipes.name: Non-sealing C query checkpoints
recipes.calls: C add 19201, global query, add 4799, global query; Rust two separate fresh instances, finished at 19201 and 24000.
recipes.observe: Compare matching prefixes rather than treating Rust finish as a reusable query.

recipes.name: Finish negative control
recipes.calls: Rust add 19201, finish, attempt add 4799. Keep separate from C query-then-continue.
recipes.observe: Source-derived expected Error::Finished; no actual call or result.
